title: Campaign ad persuasion experiments
publisher: Hewitt, Broockman, Coppock et al. · APSR 2024 · Swayable
summary: 617 real campaign ads, each tested against a control group: measured persuasion effects, hand-coded features for every ad, and 607,450 de-identified responses.
cite: Hewitt, L., Broockman, D., Coppock, A., Tappin, B., Slezak, J., Coffman, V., Lubin, N., & Hamidian, M. (2024). How Experiments Help Campaigns Persuade Voters. American Political Science Review.
can: Which coded ad features went with larger measured persuasion
How much true effects vary from ad to ad
How persuasion differs by party and gender of the viewer
cannot: The ads themselves, their transcripts, or campaign names
Paid engagement metrics like views or shares

title: PAX reference model
publisher: PAX · built from the persuasion experiments
summary: Per-feature persuasion differences from a random-effects meta-regression, the spread of true effects, and a leave-one-study-out test of how predictable an ad is from its features.
can: A prior for what a script's style is likely worth
An honest bound on how little style alone predicts

title: Small effects of political advertising
summary: 59 real-time randomized experiments on 49 presidential ads with 34,000 participants: persuasion effects by context, message, sender and receiver.
can: A second, independent estimate of typical ad effects

title: Do emotional ads persuade?
summary: Real-time campaign advertising experiments testing emotional appeals against measured persuasion.
can: Whether fear, anger or hope appeals moved viewers in tested ads

title: Upworthy headline experiments
summary: 32,487 randomized headline and image tests with click outcomes, 2013–2015: which opening line earns the click.
can: Which phrasings of an opening line win attention under randomization
cannot: Video, or whether a click changed a mind

title: Reform campaigns in Google's political ad library
publisher: Google Political Ads Transparency · via GovBlock
summary: Every open-primary and ranked-choice advertiser's Google ads: creatives, dates, impression bands, spend ranges, targeting, weekly spend and spend by state.
can: Who is spending on reform advertising, where and when
cannot: Clicks, views or persuasion (exposure bands only)

title: Reform campaign shorts
summary: About 30 recent shorts each from Vote YES on 3, Courageous Colorado, Open Primaries and Unite America, with public views, likes, comments and length.
license: Public counts; videos belong to their channels
can: Which framings campaigns are running and how they travel organically

title: Massachusetts House ballots, 2022
publisher: Klarner State Legislative Election Returns · via GovBlock
summary: How many candidates were on the 2022 general-election ballot in each of the 160 Massachusetts House districts.
can: Where a volunteer can say their representative had no opponent

title: PAX takes and video analysis
summary: Every take's video, word-level transcript, shots, on-screen text by second, timestamped video review, and measured loudness, pitch and pauses.
license: Stand-in until the partner's own videos arrive
can: What is said and shown, second by second
cannot: Real volunteers yet: these are synthetic readings

title: Polis conversations
summary: Real Polis conversations with full vote matrices: how opinion groups form and which statements bridge them.
can: The method behind consensus on Scripts

title: Political ad content codebook
summary: The standard scheme for coding political ads: sponsor, tone, issues, appeals, visuals, music.
can: A vocabulary for tagging every video the same way

title: Persuasion archive reproduction code
summary: R code that downloads, checksums and rebuilds the persuasion archive's analysis.
can: Check PAX's reference model against the authors' pipeline
